human_tolerance.notes: Wary of people in the woods but confident where food is concentrated: it feeds in pastures, visits backyard feeders and scavenges in harvested cropland. It is heavily hunted, so wild birds keep a long flight distance.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: In early spring males older than a year gobble to announce their presence to females and competing males; hens nest on the ground in a shallow scrape under cover.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Birds gather in flocks on winter range, which is how they can reach large numbers in small areas given the range of foods they exploit.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Toms gobble and display from March; peak gobbling at the start of the breeding season.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Hens lay a ground clutch of about 10-14 eggs from April.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Poults hatch after about 28 days and can fly within two weeks.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Males gobble and display from March; hens nest on the ground.

vocalizations.description: A rapid series of hollow, chuffing notes that can be heard up to a mile away, given by males to announce themselves to females and to other males in early spring; gobbling falls off in some seasons with wind, precipitation and temperature.
A sharp rising yelp, one of a large repertoire that also includes the assembly call, purr, cluck, cutt, fly-down cackle, tree call and putt.
Soft clucks and purrs that keep a flock or a hen and her poults in contact while feeding.
A sharp, single-syllable alarm 'putt' repeated as the bird stretches its neck and then runs or flies.
A low purring sound given on the ground and by a hen to her brood; 'purr, cluck' is the common combined form.
A low-pitched booming made by the movement of air in the chest air sac, like a prairie chicken, used with gobbling and spitting as a sign of social dominance and to attract females.
A sharp expulsion of air from the chest air sac, made by males alongside gobbling and drumming.
The fly-down cackle given by the flock as it comes down off the roost; a hen answers with a 'kee kee run' to call her poults in.

taxonomy.note: The record is at species level; the six recognised subspecies are not split, since the schema's id is a trinomial at most and no subspecies was needed for a Michigan locale.

external.note: ITIS TSN, NCBI taxon id and eBird code via Wikidata (P815, P685, P3444).

range.note: An upland game bird native to North America, described from Mexico; it is one of the most widely distributed galliforms, across Canada, the United States and Mexico.

traits.limb_count.note: Biped: two legs; the wings are not counted as limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walks and runs over the ground and flies when flushed; its wings are relatively small, as is typical of the galliform order.

traits.flight.note: Powered, but weak: the wings are 'relatively small, as is typical of the galliform order' with a wing chord of only 20-21.4 cm against a body of 5-11 kg.

traits.nest_type.note: Nests on the ground in a shallow scrape in dense thickets or similar cover.

traits.perching.note: Roosts on the ground and on low branches and can perch in trees, so perching is set to false here because it is not primarily a perching bird; the previewer poses cover walking and flight.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 5791.37 g converted to kilograms; Wikipedia gives 5-11 kg for an adult male, so the dataset mean sits low in that range, as expected for a mixed-sex average.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Wikipedia's 5-11 kg is the adult male range; the low end is lowered to 4 kg so the band covers typical females as well, which is judgement.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia gives 100-125 cm for an adult male; the midpoint is used, which is near the top of the range for the species as a whole because hens are much smaller.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the 1.25-1.44 m wingspan given on Wikipedia.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No allow-listed open source states wild longevity for this species. Authored estimate only: 12 years, taken as a plausible mid-range figure for a large galliform and not a sourced datum. Treat it as an order-of-magnitude value.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-PlantO 40 mapped to 'browse' (buds, leaves, fronds and roots, which Wikipedia lists), Diet-Seed 20 to 'seed', Diet-Fruit 20 to 'fruit' and Diet-Inv 20 to 'invertebrate'; the dataset classes this species as a plant-seed feeder. Mast is carried separately under habitat.resources because acorns and other tree mast are the single most cited turkey food on Wikipedia.

traits.social.note: Wild turkeys gather in flocks, and Wikipedia notes they can reach large numbers in small areas; the ceiling of 15 is authored judgement, since no open source gives a typical flock size.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0; Wikipedia describes dawn gobbling and daytime feeding in fields and pastures.

traits.defense.note: Flushes and flies from an approach, and will also run; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: The species is heavily hunted, and wild birds keep a long flight distance from people, although it feeds confidently in pastures, at feeders and in harvested cropland where food is concentrated.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value gives ground 90 / understory 10; the understory share is grouped as arboreal.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Shelters and roosts in dense thickets, scrub and forest openings, and nests on the ground.

habitat.resources.note: The three browse weights follow traits.diet; the mast, leaf-litter, ground-nesting and thicket weights are separate judgement entries, since acorns and other mast are the most-cited turkey food on Wikipedia and none of these shares is in the diet fractions.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia states it prefers hardwood and mixed conifer-hardwood forest with scattered openings such as pastures, fields, orchards and seasonal marshes, and that it often feeds in cow pastures, visits backyard feeders and favours croplands after harvest.

seasonal.strategy.note: A permanent resident on its range, with no regular migration; winter flocking is a social change rather than a movement between continents.

seasonal.phases.note: The early-spring gobbling period and the winter flocking behaviour are from Wikipedia; the calendar windows are authored judgement, since no open source gives hatching or nest dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: No allow-listed open source gives a poult growth period for this species; the 120-day juvenile window and the 0.55 scale, reflecting a small poult, are authored judgement.

vocalizations.gobble.note: Wikipedia states that males over a year old gobble in early spring to announce their presence, that the gobble carries up to a mile, and that wind, precipitation and temperature reduce it. The month window and cooldown are authored judgement. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

vocalizations.yelp.note: Wikipedia lists the plain yelp among a large repertoire of calls that also includes the assembly call, purr, cluck, cutt, fly-down cackle, tree call and putt; the wording and cooldown here are authored.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description: dark bronze-brown body, long reddish-yellow to greyish-green legs, a long dark fan-shaped tail, glossy bronze wings, and the fleshy caruncles on the head from which the species takes its name. The proportions and the tail, caruncle and snood boxes are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program. No shared program is written for large ground-feeding birds, and this is the closest fit: the species walks while foraging, flies when it flushes, and roosts overnight. Radii are scaled up well beyond the mammal default for a 5-11 kg bird that is heavily hunted, and the rest window is set for a diurnal species. Only Walk and Fly are declared as gaits, so both flee_gait and forage_gait resolve.

vocalizations.cluck.note: Contact clucks and purrs described in the article; cooldown is authored.

vocalizations.putt.note: Alarm putt described in the article; cooldown is authored.

traits.senses.note: The article credits the turkey with 'superior sight' when foraging alongside deer and squirrels that supply smell and extra eyes from the air, and describes a pigeon/hearing-like sensitivity to a flushed bird implied by the roost-flush cackle; High hearing is set on the daily flush-and-roost routine, and vibration for the strong ground contact a 6 kg walking bird has with leaf litter. No open source quantifies any sense, so the rest are omitted rather than guessed.

habitat.density_per_ha.note: Judgement: the article gives no density, only the dramatic population history. Restored populations at roughly one bird per two hectares of good habitat give typical 0.5 per hectare, and min and max are an authored tenfold band either side, following the convention used for turdus-migratorius and cardinalis-cardinalis.

vocalizations.note: The call list, the gobble audible to a mile and given by older males in early spring, weather suppressing gobbling, the air-sac drumming or booming, the 'spit', the fly-down cackle and the hen's 'kee kee run' to her poults are all quoted or closely paraphrased from the Vocalizations, Social structure and mating and roosting passages. Cooldowns and the months on the yelp and purr calls are authored judgement, since no open source quantifies them. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.
